requirement.original: Spec Item 5.16: 检修上次失败内容 — block latex 之前是好的现在被修坏了（我从未要求改 block）, inline latex 一点都没动
requirement.clarified: Re-verify LaTeX rendering on dev.life-ai.app for both inline ($...$) and block ($$...$$) cases on desktop AND mobile. Fix the residual bug: mid-line $$...$$ is currently eaten by the cycle 1 inline-$ regex, leaving stray $ characters around an inline-typeset KaTeX rendering. Canonical own-line $$...$$ and inline $...$ already pass per runtime evidence; do not regress them.
requirement.what: Add a higher-precedence $$...$$ alternative to parseMarkdownSpans regex so mid-line $$E=mc^2$$ is consumed as a single span and routed through LatexRenderer with displayMode:true; existing inline $...$ + own-line $$...$$ paths remain.
requirement.why: User claim 'block was good, now broken; inline never fixed' maps onto the mid-line $$...$$ collision the cycle 1 fix accidentally introduced; canonical cases already render correctly per BA's live runtime probe.

included: Mid-line $$...$$ recognition at the span-parser layer
MarkdownSpan type extension (latexDisplay?: boolean or equivalent discriminant)
Re-verification of inline $...$ and own-line $$...$$ on desktop + mobile
Live screenshot evidence on both viewports
excluded: LatexRenderer.tsx rendering internals (KaTeX call, CSS, native WebView)
Multi-line mid-line $$...$$ where the closing $$ is on a different line and surrounded by prose

success_criteria: Mid-line $$E=mc^2$$ produces one .katex element and zero raw $ chars in the message body innerText
Own-line $$E=mc^2$$ continues to produce a .katex-display element
Inline $a^2+b^2=c^2$ continues to produce a .katex element with correct annotation and no raw $
Both desktop (1280x720) and mobile (390x844) viewports verified with screenshots
constraints: Do NOT modify LatexRenderer rendering internals
Do NOT modify parseMarkdownBlock.ts (block path stays own-line-only by design)
Build must come from the worktree, not /root/happy
Verification must use Playwright on dev.life-ai.app, not curl/HTTP

root_cause_analysis.symptom: User perceives 'block latex broken, inline never fixed'. Live DOM probe shows canonical demo (inline $a^2+b^2=c^2$ + own-line $$E=mc^2$$) renders 4 .katex elements correctly. Cycle 1 QA report flagged the residual mid-line $$...$$ collision as 'pass-with-note'.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: parseMarkdownSpans.ts:6 inline $...$ regex (added in cycle 1, commit 0ba2ddfc) consumes the inner $E=mc^2$ of any mid-line $$E=mc^2$$ token because parseMarkdownBlock.ts only handles $$ when trimmed.startsWith('$$'). Net effect: mid-line $$...$$ renders as $ <KaTeX inline> $ with two surplus $ glyphs.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: 0ba2ddfc - 'feat: cycle 1 (14 pipelines) + close-remediation' (2026-04-24, see also ba-spec-20260424-143000-1.md and qa-report-20260424-143000-1.json)
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Cycle 1 BA spec for §5.16 explicitly scoped to inline $...$; block $$...$$ was assumed unaffected because parseMarkdownBlock.ts path is independent. The interaction with mid-line $$...$$ was not anticipated.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Span regex now matches the inner $...$ of any $$...$$ that fails the block path's startsWith('$$') guard. Outer $ markers leak into rendered text; user reads this as 'block broken'.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Block path introduced 2026-03-23 (f8b208fa); inline path added 2026-04-24 23:22 UTC (0ba2ddfc); user complaint surfaced 2026-04-25 ~14:50 (Section 4 Correction line 2810).
observations: Same probe at 390x844 mobile: 4 .katex elements, identical annotation textContent, identical computed display values (observed)
Inline .katex bounding box: 100x22 px, fontFamily KaTeX_Main, display:inline (observed via getBoundingClientRect + getComputedStyle)
Block .katex bounding box: 348x24 px (desktop) / 292x24 px (mobile), display:block (observed)
<annotation> computed display === 'none' (observed, KaTeX hides accessibility text)
document.body.innerText.indexOf('$$E') === -1 (observed, no raw block $$ leak on canonical demo)
parseMarkdownSpans.ts:6 regex contains group 10-11 alternative '(\$([^\s$][^$\n]*?[^\s$]|[^\s$\d\\])\$)' for inline $...$ (inferred from source read)
parseMarkdownBlock.ts:150 'if (!trimmed.startsWith("$$")) return false;' restricts block path to lines that begin with $$ (inferred)

qa-report-20260424-143000-1.json 'additional_acceptance_checks[0]' explicitly notes mid-line $$...$$ produces '$ [KaTeX(E=mc^2)] $' with two stray $ — this is the residual bug (observed historical evidence)
root_cause_analysis.localization_evidence: Reproduced live on https://dev.life-ai.app/session/cmoedofgz86n5nz15xsldnk35 with Playwright at desktop 1280x720 and mobile 390x844. browser_evaluate confirmed 4 .katex elements (2 inline, 2 display) with correct annotation textContent and KaTeX CSS loaded. Source-walked the rendering pipeline: parseMarkdownSpans.ts (inline regex), parseMarkdownBlock.ts (block startsWith guard), MarkdownView.tsx (dispatch), LatexRenderer.tsx (KaTeX call). The mid-line $$...$$ bug is provable by source reading + cycle 1 QA report's pass-with-note (the QA explicitly observed the stray $ behaviour during cycle 1 verification).

pre_existing_guards.purpose: Reject escaped \$ from being treated as LaTeX delimiter
Reject $ that follows an alphanumeric character (e.g. word$ continuation) from being a LaTeX opening
Inline $...$ content cannot start/end with whitespace; single-character content cannot be a digit (rejects $1/$5/$100); cannot be a backslash (rejects \$ continuation)
Block $$...$$ matches only when the line begins with $$. KEEP — this is the contract that distinguishes block from inline; removing it would conflict with the new span-level $$ matcher.

novelty_check.rationale: Same L4 file (parseMarkdownSpans.ts) and same regex layer, but a different sub-dimension: this attempt adds a higher-precedence \$\$...\$\$ alternative ANCHORED IN FRONT OF the existing \$...\$ alternative + a new latexDisplay span discriminant. Attempt 1 (f8b208fa) was block-only. Attempt 2 (0ba2ddfc) was inline-only and its regex did not anticipate the $$...$$ collision. This attempt explicitly resolves the $$/$ precedence collision and threads displayMode:true through a new span variant — neither prior attempt touched precedence or the variant dimension. Not a duplicate.
